title: A fault-tolerant neutral-atom architecture for universal quantum computation (Bluvstein, Lukin et al.)
key_claim: Reconfigurable arrays of up to 448 neutral atoms implement the key elements of a universal, fault-tolerant quantum processing architecture; demonstrates 2.14(13)x below-threshold performance in a four-round characterization circuit, and deep-circuit protocols with dozens of logical qubits and hundreds of logical teleportations using high-rate [[16,6,4]] codes. Published online 10 November 2025; Publisher Correction 19 January 2026; print Nature volume 649, pages 39-46 (2026).
notes: Structural anchor. Canonical Tier 1 primary research establishing the neutral-atom fault-tolerant architecture framing. Cited at the January 2026 corrected/print version. WebFetch verified, abstract and metadata retrieved.

title: Computing with many encoded logical qubits beyond break-even (arXiv:2602.22211)
key_claim: Demonstrates beyond-break-even computation with between 48 and 94 logical qubits on the 98-qubit Quantinuum Helios trapped-ion processor using high-rate iceberg quantum error-detecting and two-level concatenated iceberg QEC codes; 94-logical-qubit GHZ state at ~94.9% fidelity; logical gate error rates roughly one error in ten thousand operations.
notes: Tier 1 primary research preprint from a recognised institution. Submitted 25 February 2026. WebFetch confirmed URL resolves; submission date and abstract corroborated via WebSearch (arXiv listing, ADS, The Quantum Insider).

title: McKinsey Quantum Technology Monitor 2026: A commercial tipping point
key_claim: Fifth annual monitor; quantum investment surged to $12.6 billion in 2025, a 6.3-fold year-on-year increase; roughly 60% of 2025 investment concentrated in the top ten deals; private investment accounted for 97% of funding versus 67% in 2024; over 300 companies actively collaborating with quantum technology firms. Data collection ended March 2026.
notes: Tier 2 institutional consultancy research. Existence and figures cross-verified via WebSearch and the PostQuantum.com analysis which links directly to the McKinsey page; mckinsey.de press release corroborates. Direct WebFetch returned a JS-rendered shell.

title: Google Quantum AI Engages JILA Fellow Adam Kaufman to Lead New Neutral Atom Quantum Computing Effort
key_claim: Google Quantum AI named JILA Fellow Adam Kaufman to lead a newly formed neutral-atom quantum hardware team based in Boulder; described as Google's first large-scale investment in neutral-atom quantum computing, complementing its long-standing superconducting work.
notes: Tier 2 academic-institution announcement from the joint CU Boulder / NIST institute directly involved. WebFetch verified, full content retrieved.

title: Google Paves a Two-Lane Quantum Roadmap by Adding Neutral Atom Systems
key_claim: Google Quantum AI, a superconducting pioneer, is adding a neutral-atom modality; superconducting cycles take about a microsecond while neutral-atom cycles take milliseconds, but neutral-atom arrays have reached roughly 10,000 qubits with any-to-any connectivity; the move reflects a growing industry view that no single hardware approach will dominate near-term.
notes: Tier 3 specialist journalism. WebFetch verified, full content retrieved.

title: Quantinuum Researchers Demonstrate Quantum Computations With Dozens of Protected Logical Qubits
key_claim: Quantinuum demonstrated up to 94 error-detected and 48 error-corrected logical qubits from 98 physical qubits on the Helios trapped-ion processor with beyond-break-even performance; flexible-connectivity architectures (trapped-ion and neutral-atom) are noted as particularly well-suited to high-rate iceberg codes; the work still relies in part on postselection and is not yet fully fault-tolerant.
notes: Tier 3 specialist journalism summarising arXiv:2602.22211; also carries the partial-fault-tolerance and postselection caveats used in the counter-argument. WebFetch verified, full content retrieved.

title: McKinsey Quantum Technology Monitor 2026: 'A Commercial Tipping Point' - But the Numbers Deserve Scrutiny
key_claim: Independent analysis of the McKinsey monitor argues quantum is in a 'messy middle' between research curiosity and commercial technology; most applications remain experimental or hybrid; the $12.6bn investment figure is 'directionally correct but precisely wrong'; IBM's 2029 fault-tolerance timeline is 'technically possible but practically uncertain'; scaling bottlenecks are mundane engineering (lasers, cryogenics, control electronics, manufacturing).
notes: Tier 3 independent expert commentary; principal sourced counter-evidence for the Counter-Argument. Treated directionally. WebFetch verified, full content retrieved.

title: Building superconducting and neutral atom quantum computers (Hartmut Neven)
key_claim: Google states superconducting processors are easier to scale in circuit depth while neutral atoms are easier to scale in qubit count, and that 'investing in both approaches increases our ability to deliver on our mission, sooner'; commercially relevant superconducting machines still expected by the end of the decade.
notes: Tier 4 vendor disclosure; used directionally to evidence the incumbent's own hedge. WebFetch verified, full content retrieved.
